title: The most underrated line in any itinerary.
subtitle: Overnight in port. Two words that change what the whole voyage feels like.

text: A ship that stays the night gives you the town twice.
sub: Once in the afternoon, when it belongs to the day-trippers and the fleet. And once at nine in the evening, when it belongs to the people who live there.

title: Four things an overnight gives you

items.head: Dinner ashore, unhurried
items.body: No all-aboard hanging over the second course. The best meal of most voyages happens exactly this way.

items.head: The town after the fleet leaves
items.body: Harbour towns exhale around seven. The tavernas fill with locals and nothing at all is queued.

items.head: A morning with no gangway rush
items.body: You wake already there. Coffee at eight in a square that is still being swept.

items.head: Weather margin
items.body: Two windows instead of one. A tender port with an overnight is a far safer promise than one without.

points.value: One afternoon, shared with every other ship in the harbour.

points.label: Arrive 14:00
points.value: Half the town shut for the afternoon; you queue for the other half.

points.label: Overnight, day one
points.value: Afternoon, dinner ashore, and then the empty morning after it.

points.label: Depart 13:00, day two
points.value: A late lunch on deck as the island goes back to being itself.

quote: The best evening I can put in an itinerary costs nothing extra. It is simply a ship that doesn't leave.

title: Save this for the next itinerary you're sent.
body: Then look for the word *overnight*. If it isn't there, ask me whether a sailing exists that has one - in most seasons and most regions, there is.
